about: The estimator's Master Template as data: how each system looks, which line to pick when, and tech hours. Guidance, not a mandatory point list. Edit here, never in code. Words in a condition are matched as whole words, ignoring case; a condition holds when any one of its words is found in any one of its places. Job details the template's samples carry (tag lists, 'Qty. N Total', valve sizes, sheet references, floor locations) are left out of the line texts: the writer adds the job's own.
integration_trio: Furnish BMS Communication Wiring to {what} Factory Controls
Map Available Points Via Mfr. Provided BMS Interface
AME requires mfr. Rep to assist in integration, cost to be incurred by mech contractor

placeholders.{what}: the equipment named in the first integration line (Chiller, Pump VFD, ...); empty for plain factory controls
placeholders.{unit}: the unit an alarm is watched at (HVAC alarm panel)

client_note_examples: **Refrigeration Leak Detection system is coming with the unit per equipment schedule

factory_controls.about: When the unit comes with the manufacturer's own controls, the three integration lines replace the lines that name a DDC controller. The words are looked for, whole and ignoring case, in the schedule's who-provides-the-controller notes, its other notes and its cells.

counted_devices.about: For a line whose quantity is counted, the device labels on the plans that count it (the labels are in reading_lists/devices.json). The line matches when it contains the words on the left, ignoring case; the longest match wins. A line with no match, or no label counted on the system's sheets, falls back to one per unit, as an assumption.
